why: A method that halves variance but triples run time is a loss.

q: A method halves variance but makes each run 3× slower. What is its efficiency relative to plain sampling at equal time? (ratio, below 1 means worse)
why: Plain sampling gets 3× the runs, cutting variance 3×; the method cuts it 2×: 2/3.

q: Antithetic variates pair each uniform draw u with …
why: The mirror draw; for normals the mirror of z is −z.
Myth. They help for monotone models; for a symmetric (non-monotone) function they can increase variance.

q: A control variate has correlation 0.9 with the output. Variance falls to what fraction of the original?

why: The correction uses C − E[C], so E[C] must be known exactly.

o: each input's N strata each get exactly one point
why: It stratifies every input separately and shuffles the strata across inputs.

q: Why scramble and repeat a Sobol (quasi-Monte Carlo) run?
o: to get an honest error estimate from the spread
why: One deterministic sequence gives no spread; independent scrambles do.

q: Which method suits estimating a 1-in-a-million loss probability?
why: It samples where the event happens and reweights, saving orders of magnitude.

q: A warning sign of a bad importance sampling proposal is …
o: a few draws carrying most of the total weight
why: Heavy weights on a few draws mean the estimate can jump when a new large weight appears.
